## Design

### 2026-10-03 — ![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/b022a2e26d8eaaebc1e1671d53c9547494f0e923b594a446180a9affb7dd2cbd.png)My split ergo keyboard p

**3h**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/b022a2e26d8eaaebc1e1671d53c9547494f0e923b594a446180a9affb7dd2cbd.png)My split ergo keyboard project — how it's going

KiCad and the libraries

I set up KiCad 10.0.6 and realized I was missing the kicad-library package — the one that ships all the symbols and footprints. That's why I kept getting that "library table not found" error when I opened the libraries window. Once I installed it, everything clicked into place.

I also grabbed the ScottoKicad library (Joe Scotto's, the go-to for handwired keyboards)

Nailing down what I want

I figured out the design as I went and jotted it down in docs/requirements.md:

- Wired (USB), no wireless.
- Spanish ISO layout: Ñ, accent marks, ç/Ç, ¡, ¿, the whole set.
- No numpad (don't use it).
- One single PCB that I split into two halves afterwards (V-cut / mouse bites) so I only order one board from JLCPCB.
- 37+37 keys, symmetric.
- OLED 128x32 on the left + EC11 encoder on the right.
- 2× RP2040-Zero, using the USB-C that already comes on the board itself (no hubs or extra receptacles).

Hunting down components

- 90 switches Outemu Silent Lemon V3 (silent tactile, so I don't annoy everyone at home)
- 2 RP2040-Zero.
- OLED, encoder, TRRS jacks

The layout in KLE

I ended up designing the layout to my liking in Keyboard Layout Editor:

My layout

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/9bcd3b6019fe6ba5625c8275abcca2e4b4507b177681d32380b8e2a8736c0e92.png)
It's a split columnar-stagger in Spanish, ~37–45 keys per half, split spacebar, thumb clusters, and dedicated arrows on the right. Pretty happy with how it turned out.

The BOM and the repo

- Put together the BOM (docs/bom.md) with the full part list: ~€34 of electronics.
- Updated the README with the layout image and where the project stands.

My whole project is actually inspired by my main keyboard, the Logitech G513 Carbon — I've been using it for ages and it works great. But I wanted to take a simple step toward this new kind of keyboard, the ergonomic split, without leaving everything else behind.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/57616758888f32023ba3507fd8a373186508a66b0327d43de8ec44e9d9466df4.png)

### 2026-10-04 — Hit a wall today, but figured it out. Turns out the layout I had originally was misplaced — the columns weren't lined up right, so it wasn't actually symmetric after all. That bugged me, so I redid th

**4h**

Hit a wall today, but figured it out. Turns out the layout I had originally was misplaced — the columns weren't lined up right, so it wasn't actually symmetric after all. That bugged me, so I redid the whole thing from scratch.![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/e9ec58fceb7e9e92f52a324955255ef5ec6a7692dff6cc3a577f8f2d2e38f523.png)
And I actually got the whole schematic done! Switches + diodes matrix, both halves wired, the RP2040-Zero(s), the OLED, the TRRS jacks, and the encoder all placed and connected. Fixed the footprints as I went (diodes were wrongly grabbing the encoder footprint, etc.), sorted the "Update PCB from Schematic" thing, and dealt with the harmless mounting-pad warnings. Schematic is done and clean.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/BHVSotWnbG2fhKlROyX6D3uJ45kKD2Lz/b3904226ba8c6458d84470f6642ab97eb67101f1a248d40e09c38332544f8bda.png)
Now the new problem: I need to get this layout out of KLE and into the actual PCB. That's the part that's stressing me. I'm looking at either passing it to Ergogen (the web tool that generates the board for you) or finding some other way to convert it — and then I still have to figure out how to place all the switches in KiCad without dying of boredom doing it one by one.
